findings.issue: Twenty new lemmas restate, at a fixed relation, generic lemmas added in the same PR, and have no consumer anywhere in the repository (verified by grepping each name over TauCeti/): ICenter_def (85), ICenter_empty_left (92), ICenter_empty_right (97), ICenter_singleton_singleton (102), ICenter_union_left (117), ICenter_union_right (122), ICenter_insert_left (127), ICenter_insert_right (132), ICenter_image_swap (138); JNumCenter_empty_left (207), JNumCenter_empty_right (212), JNumCenter_union_left (230), JNumCenter_union_right (236), JNumCenter_insert_left (241), JNumCenter_insert_right (246); JCenter_empty_left (268), JCenter_empty_right (273), JCenter_union_left (293), JCenter_union_right (298), JCenter_insert_right (308). Each proof is a single application of the located generic lemma (e.g. `ICenter_union_left := Icount_union_left _ h`, `JCenter_union_left := JCount_union_left _ _ h`), so the block is a parallel API over `GridPoint.Icount`/`JNumCount`/`JCount` rather than new mathematics. Note `JFunction/Basic.lean` already carries the same mirror layer for `I`/`JNum`/`J`, so this is the third copy of the same seven-lemma shape.

summary: The relation-parametric refactor is sound and the strict-`J` API is correctly re-derived from it, but `JFunction/Center.lean` also adds ~20 consumer-less mirror lemmas that are literally the generic `Icount_*`/`JNumCount_*`/`JCount_*` lemmas applied at a fixed relation. Delete the ones with no caller; the rest of the PR reuses existing API well.
